subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron runs get an explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep the current per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards model?
rationale: This defines a scheduled-run security boundary and public config precedence contract, so automation should not choose the default or upgrade behavior without maintainer product/security intent.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against current policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus focused cron delivery regression tests.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Make cron sessions reuse `tools.subagents.tools` semantics, accepting the simpler config surface while documenting any compatibility impact on existing jobs.

options.title: Keep current model
options.body: Decline the new config surface and document per-job `--tools`, creator-derived `toolsAllow`, and delivery safeguards as the supported mitigation.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against current policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus focused cron delivery regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-source and issue-review history for the shared config and tool-policy boundary.
